articles.title: Oil spill from grounded tanker reaches Oman’s mainland beaches
articles.summary: France 24 reports that leaked crude from the grounded tanker *Caroline Bezengi* has now reached mainland beaches in Oman, escalating a spill that Omani authorities said covered about 390–400 square kilometers and lay within roughly 7 kilometers of the coast. The tanker, which is believed to have loaded close to a million barrels of Russian oil and has been stranded since early June after a suspected onboard blast, sits near the Al Hallaniyat archipelago inside a protected marine area. The spill is significant because it threatens sensitive coastal ecosystems, including marine life around Qibliyah Island, and raises concerns that oil could reach shallower waters, the shoreline, and nearby infrastructure such as desalination plants and tourism sites.

articles.title: ICE plans to outfit officers with electric shock gloves
articles.summary: Immigration and Customs Enforcement is planning to spend about $10 million to $20 million on electric shock gloves called the G.L.O.V.E. — short for Generated Low Output Voltage Emitter — for officers in Homeland Security Investigations and Enforcement Removal Operations. The gloves, made by Kentucky-based Compliant Technologies, are designed to deliver a painful shock through direct skin contact to stop a person from making coordinated muscle movements, but the manufacturer’s manual says they should not be used against verbal defiance or as punishment, and warns against using them on children, pregnant women, the elderly, or people with serious disabilities. DHS’s notice suggests a no-bid contract could be published as soon as Friday, and ICE could begin fielding the gloves by March, which has prompted sharp criticism from civil rights and immigrant-rights groups who argue the device adds another potentially abusive use-of-force tool to immigration enforcement.

articles.title: White House press secretary and Trump adviser Karoline Leavitt to leave role

Trump said Leavitt has been a strong spokeswoman and will remain one of his top outside advisers, keeping an influential role in his orbit even after stepping down. The move matters because Leavitt has been one of Trump’s most visible and trusted communications figures since his return to office in January 2025, so her departure marks a notable personnel shift in the White House press operation.

The DHS says the goal is to give agents equipment to safely apprehend and remove people it describes as criminal illegal aliens, while critics note the shocks can be administered in a way that may not be obvious to bystanders. The story matters because it shows ICE moving toward a more concealed use-of-force tool, raising questions about transparency, training, and how such technology will be used in immigration enforcement.

It explains that warming ocean waters are disrupting plankton and pushing sardines into deeper, cooler waters, which has reduced catches and left processing plants short of fish; the shortage is especially severe in Morocco, a major supplier to North American and European grocery stores. The piece also notes that bad weather, high fuel costs, and fishing limits imposed to protect wild stocks have made it even harder for suppliers to increase production, so the empty shelves are likely to persist for a while. This matters because sardines have gone from a cheap pantry staple to a trendy tinned-fish item, and the article shows how climate stress and consumer hype can quickly expose fragility in global food supply chains.

articles.title: Stop Pretending To Do Domain-Driven Design

articles.title: HTML over WebSockets: real-time SPAs with barely any JavaScript
articles.summary: The article argues for building real-time single-page apps by sending **HTML over WebSockets** instead of JSON, so the server renders the markup and the browser mostly just inserts it into the DOM. It frames this as part of the broader “hypermedia” or “HTML over the wire” approach, with the key advantage being lower latency and true bidirectional communication: the persistent WebSocket connection avoids repeated HTTP handshakes and lets the server push updates immediately when state changes. The author emphasizes that this can produce SPAs with very little JavaScript, one backend language, no separate API contract, and simpler rendering logic because the backend owns the templates and business logic. Why it matters is that it offers a practical alternative for apps that need live interaction—such as chat, collaboration, or games—while also noting the tradeoff that keeping one WebSocket open per client increases server resource usage and the ecosystem is still relatively young.

articles.title: Tailscale Traces Database Corruption to 16y/o SQLite WAL-Reset Bug
articles.summary: Tailscale says repeated corruption outages in its control plane were ultimately traced to SQLite’s 16-year-old “WAL-reset bug,” a rare race condition in WAL mode where a checkpoint and a write transaction collide and SQLite mistakenly believes pages from the WAL have already been copied into the main database file. When that happens, data can be permanently lost and the database can become corrupt because indexes or other pages point to records that were never actually written. Tailscale helped SQLite developers reproduce the issue by adding extra logging via a new tmstmpvfs shim, and SQLite fixed it by adding a checkpoint check that detects when another thread has reset the WAL. The incident mattered because it showed the bug was not just theoretical: Tailscale’s own production alert confirmed the exact overlap still happened in real deployments, and after deploying the fix the company reported months without further database incidents.

It also notes a subtle rightward bias in the resampling output, especially as the scale factor increases. This matters because web developers who rely on tiny JPEGs or CSS resizing may see browser-dependent rendering differences, so image quality can change even when the file itself is the same.

articles.title: React 19's useFormStatus Fixed My Prop Drilling. Then It Sat There Returning False
articles.summary: The article argues that React 19’s `useFormStatus` solves prop drilling for form loading states by letting any descendant inside a `<form>` read the nearest form’s live submission status without passing `isPending` or `loading` props through intermediate components. It shows the practical payoff: reusable submit buttons and spinners can automatically disable or update themselves during submission, especially with Server Actions, instead of relying on manual state plumbing. The author also highlights the main limitation that caused the hook to “sit there returning false” in their case—`useFormStatus` only works when the component is rendered inside the form boundary, so using it in the same component that creates the `<form>` will not see the status. That matters because it clarifies when to use `useFormStatus` versus `useActionState`: the former is for live in-progress UI, while the latter is for the result of the submission, such as validation errors or success messages.
